sources.text:
Vézelay Abbey (French: Abbaye Sainte-Marie-Madeleine de Vézelay) is a Benedictine and Cluniac monastery in Vézelay in the east-central French department of Yonne.  It was constructed between 1120 and 1150. The Benedictine abbey church, now the Basilica of Sainte-Marie-Madeleine (Saint Mary Magdalene), with its complex program of imagery in sculpted capitals and portals, is one of the great masterpieces of Burgundian Romanesque art and architecture. Sacked by the Huguenots in 1569, the building suffered from neglect in the 17th and the 18th centuries and further damage during the French Revolution.
The church and hill at Vézelay were added to the UNESCO list of World Heritage Sites in 1979 because of their importance in medieval Christianity and outstanding architecture. Relics of Mary Magdalene can be seen inside the Basilica.


== History ==


=== Early history ===
The Benedictine abbey was founded on land that had been a late Roman villa, of Vercellus (Vercelle becoming Vézelay). The villa had passed into the hands of the Carolingians and devolved to a Carolingian count, Girart, of Roussillon. Die Benediktinerabteikirche, heute die Basilika Sainte-Marie-Madeleine, ist mit ihrem komplexen Bildprogramm an skulptierten Kapitellen und Portalen eines der großen Meisterwerke der burgundischen romanischen Kunst und Architektur. 1569 von den Hugenotten geplündert, litt das Gebäude im 17. und 18. Jahrhundert unter Vernachlässigung und erlitt während der Französischen Revolution weitere Schäden.
